# `regex`

The `regex` module (`#use regex`) implements a linear-time regular expression engine based on Russ Cox's **Thompson NFA / PikeVM** virtual machine. Because active NFA states are deduplicated at every byte position, matching runs in guaranteed $O(N \times M)$ time with zero catastrophic backtracking (ReDoS-immune), zero external C dependencies, and full compatibility across Linux, macOS, Windows, and `wasm32-unknown-unknown`.

## Types

| Type | Fields | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Regex` | `(pattern: String, prog: Instr{}, num_groups: Int, anchored_start: <>)` | Compiled PikeVM regular expression program |
| `Span` | `(start: Int, end: Int, text: String)` | Substring span (`start == -1` when an optional capture group did not participate) |
| `Match` | `(start: Int, end: Int, text: String, groups: Span{})` | Full match span plus all capture groups (`groups(0)` is the full match, `groups(1..N)` are numbered captures) |

## Pattern Syntax

| Construct | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `.` | Any byte except `\n` (or any byte when `(?s)` is active) |
| `^` / `$` | Start / end of input (or start / end of line when `(?m)` is active) |
| `\A` / `\z` | Start / end of input |
| `\b` / `\B` | ASCII word boundary (`[A-Za-z0-9_]`) / non-word boundary |
| `*`, `+`, `?` | Greedy quantifiers: `0+`, `1+`, `0..1` |
| `*?`, `+?`, `??` | Lazy (non-greedy) quantifiers |
| `{m}`, `{m,}`, `{m,n}` | Bounded quantifiers up to 256 (append `?` for lazy `{m,n}?`) |
| `a\|b` | Leftmost-first alternation |
| `(...)` | Numbered capture group (`1..N`) |
| `(?:...)` | Non-capturing group |
| `(?ims)` / `(?ims:...)` | Inline flags: `i` (case-insensitive), `m` (multiline `^`/`$`), `s` (dotall `.`) |
| `[...]` / `[^...]` | Character class / negated character class (`[a-z0-9_-]`, `[^\s]`) |
| `\d`, `\D` | ASCII digit `[0-9]` / non-digit `[^0-9]` |
| `\w`, `\W` | ASCII word `[A-Za-z0-9_]` / non-word `[^A-Za-z0-9_]` |
| `\s`, `\S` | Whitespace `[ \t\n\r\f\v]` / non-whitespace |
| `\n`, `\r`, `\t`, `\xHH` | Control & hexadecimal byte escapes |

## Public API

| Function | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `compile` | `String => < Regex \| Error >` | Compiles a pattern into a PikeVM `Regex` |
| `match` | `#! P: Type, P, String => <>` | Returns `<+>` if `pat` (`Regex` or pattern `String`) matches anywhere in `text` |
| `find` | `Regex, String => < Match >` | Finds the first match of `re` in `text` |
| `find_at` | `Regex, String, Int => < Match >` | Finds the first match starting at or after `start_pos` |
| `find_all` | `Regex, String => Match{}` | Finds all non-overlapping matches of `re` in `text` |
| `captures` | `Regex, String => < String{} >` | Returns `[full, group1, group2, ...]` for the first match |
| `replace` | `Regex, String, String => String` | Replaces first match (`$$`, `$&`, `$0`, `$1`..`$9` supported) |
| `replace_all` | `Regex, String, String => String` | Replaces all non-overlapping matches |
| `replace_with` | `Regex, String, (Match => String) => String` | Replaces all matches using a callback `Match => String` |
| `split` | `Regex, String => String{}` | Splits `text` around all matches of `re` |
| `split_n` | `Regex, String, Int => String{}` | Splits `text` into at most `max_parts` parts |
| `escape` | `String => String` | Escapes all regex metacharacters in a literal string |

## Examples

### Matching, Capture Groups, and SemVer Extraction

```{.dva .run}
#use io
#use regex

re = regex::compile("v?(\\d+)\\.(\\d+)\\.(\\d+)(?:-([0-9A-Za-z.-]+))?")!!
caps = regex::captures(re, "release v1.4.6-rc.2")!!
io::out("full:  " + caps(0)!!)
io::out("major: " + caps(1)!!)
io::out("minor: " + caps(2)!!)
io::out("patch: " + caps(3)!!)
io::out("pre:   " + caps(4)!!)
```

### Greedy vs. Lazy Quantifiers, Replacement, and Splitting

```{.dva .run}
#use io
#use regex

// Lazy quantifier <.+?> matches each individual tag
re_tag = regex::compile("<.+?>")!!
tags = regex::find_all(re_tag, "<b>Edva</b> <i>PikeVM</i>")
io::out(?tags)

// Group-aware replacement with $1 and $2
re_kv = regex::compile("(\\w+)=(\\d+)")!!
io::out(regex::replace_all(re_kv, "x=10, y=20", "$1:$2"))

// Splitting by whitespace-padded delimiter
re_sep = regex::compile("\\s*;\\s*")!!
parts = regex::split(re_sep, "alpha ; beta;  gamma")
io::out(parts(1)!!)
```
